Anthony Fenech
Tigers beat writer
Detroit Free Press
(734) 752-9667
Twitter: @anthonyfenech
From: John Lowe <johnlowe86@gmail.com>
Sent: Wednesday, September 23, 2015 8:49 PM
To: Fenech, Anthony <afenech@freepress.com>
Subject: Fwd: Costas mini-masterpiece
I think you told me you didn't see this because you were getting ready for "your late local news." So here is this Costas clip, along with what I just sent to our sportscasting students:
When you're on the air live, you don't have time to google anything. If you want to talk about history as it happens, you have to know it. Or at least have a sense of it.

Please watch the clip from Bob Costas at the bottom of this e-mail. It comes moments after Tony Romo led the Cowboys down the field in the final minute and beat the Giants. Romo threw the winning touchdown pass with seven seconds to play.

In the midst of hosting the post-game show, Costas gets a fact from the statistician in the truck: It's the latest in the fourth quarter a Cowboys quarterback has thrown a game-winning touchdown pass.
Costas could have delievered this information in a one-sentence monotone.
You might say, "That's Bob Costas. He's a veteran. He has covered a lot of this history. He has been on the air a lot. I can't do that."

But you can. A performance like this comes from liking history and knowing history; of sensing a story and knowing how to tell one spontaneously. As you watch Costas' eyes, you can see him literally search his mind for the names of the Cowboys quarterbacks. He doesn't just tell the story. He unspools it. He unfolds it. Listen to the emphasis he puts on each name.
To show that your historical frame of reference can extend before your lifetime, look at Costas' statement in the final two sentences of this story.
Neither of the players he mentions has appeared in a big-league game in the last 99 years.
As always, I'm open to questions and conversation. Please let me know if you have a topic you'd like me to address.
